extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, USPTO/OED staff, and parties interested in USPTO disciplinary actions
extracted.subtask_description: An Office of Enrollment & Discipline (OED) Final Order describing disciplinary findings, the regulatory provisions violated (37 C.F.R. pt. 11), sanctions imposed (suspension, probation, monitor), and publication/monitoring requirements for a suspended USPTO-registered patent attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Practice Monitor confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall take reasonable steps to ensure that, whenever the Patent Practice Monitor views confidential client information, the practice monitor understands and agrees that such matters are to remain confidential pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.106;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation applies whenever the monitor views confidential client information; monitor must understand and agree to confidentiality consistent with 37 C.F.R. § 11.106 (client confidentiality/privilege protections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic publication of Final Order (OED FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room, which is publicly accessible through the Office's website at: https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final disciplinary orders are to be made publicly accessible via the OED FOIA Reading Room (electronic publication requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice publication (materially consistent text)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the following: Notice of Suspension and Probation [text summarizing respondent, suspension term, probation, monitor requirement, and the rule violations].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must materially match the provided template, summarizing sanction (suspension, probation, monitor requirement) and the rule citations supporting the discipline; used to inform the registered practitioner community/public.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 — Lack of competence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples supporting this violation in the order include numerous filing mistakes, failures in prosecution steps, and errors that harmed clients (e.g., mistakes in filing non‑provisional applications resulting in loss of provisional benefit).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — Lack of diligence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order cites repeated failures to act diligently, including not replying to Office communications and not taking timely actions on client matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2),(a)(3),(b) — Inadequate communication with clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation cited: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2), (a)(3), and (b) (inadequate communication with clients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific examples: respondent repeatedly failed to communicate despite clients' numerous attempts; in some cases gave inaccurate/false/misleading information about the status of patent applications (e.g., telling clients applications were still pending when they had been abandoned).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(a) & (c) — Failure to safekeep client property
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation cited: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(a) & (c) (failure to safekeep client property).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order lists failure to safekeep client property among grounds for discipline; the document does not elaborate specific facts here beyond its inclusion in the rule-violation list.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) — Conduct involving misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation cited: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) (engaging in conduct involving misrepresentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order supports this with concrete instances of providing inaccurate, false, or misleading information to clients about their application status (e.g., asserting applications were pending when they had been abandoned).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions imposed — suspension, probation, and monitor requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has suspended Mr. Cann from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent-related matters for a period of twenty-four (24) months; placed him on probation; and ordered that Mr. Cann obtain a Patent Practice Monitor upon being reinstated to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the disciplinary disposition: a 24‑month suspension across PTO practice, concurrent probation, and a condition of reinstatement requiring a Patent Practice Monitor to oversee future practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harm from filing errors (loss of provisional benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent made mistakes when filing clients' patent applications and in two instances made mistakes in connection with filing the non-provisional patent application resulting in the loss of the benefit of the filing date from their provisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order uses these concrete adverse outcomes as evidence of incompetence/diligence failures and as an example of professional harm to clients.
